description: Securing your first residents, working with placement agencies, and optional Medi-Cal ALW enrollment.

sections.title: Marketing & Resident Intake
sections.summary: Strategies and legal requirements for admitting private-pay residents into your RCFE.

bullets.label: Contract with Placement Agencies
bullets.detail: Establish referral agreements with agencies like 'A Place for Mom' or local senior placement specialists. Standard referral fees are typically 50-100% of the first month's rent.

bullets.label: Execute the Admission Agreement
bullets.detail: Sign the formal contract with the resident or their responsible party. It must strictly adhere to the admission policies approved by CDSS in your Part B application.

bullets.label: Obtain Physician's Report (LIC 602A)
bullets.detail: Before admission, ensure the prospective resident has a completed LIC 602A signed by a physician detailing their medical needs, TB clearance, and ambulatory status.

bullets.label: Complete Needs and Services Plan
bullets.detail: Conduct a pre-admission appraisal to evaluate the resident's physical, cognitive, and social needs, and create a formal plan to accommodate them.

sections.title: Assisted Living Waiver (ALW) - Optional
sections.summary: The process to become a Medi-Cal provider to accept subsidized residents.

bullets.label: Obtain your RCFE License First
bullets.detail: You cannot apply for the ALW program until your facility is fully licensed by CDSS.

bullets.label: Submit ALW Provider Application
bullets.detail: Apply through the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) to become an enrolled Medi-Cal provider for the Assisted Living Waiver program.

bullets.label: Contract with Care Coordination Agencies (CCAs)
bullets.detail: Once approved, partner with regional CCAs who assess eligible Medi-Cal beneficiaries and place them into ALW-approved facilities.

sections.title: Post-Licensing Compliance
sections.summary: Crucial regulatory steps immediately following the issuance of your license.

bullets.label: Hire and Clear Staff
bullets.detail: Before any staff member begins work, they must pass their live scan background check, obtain a health screening/TB test, and complete their required initial training.

bullets.label: Prepare for the 90-Day Inspection
bullets.detail: An LPA will conduct an unannounced visit within the first 90 days of operation to ensure you are actively following Title 22 regulations and your approved Plan of Operation.
